scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Circle of Light: Thiruvathirakkali
This is Thiruvathirakkali. Ancient to modern.
on_screen: Title card: Thiruvathirakkali · India · Ancient to modern

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance has ancient roots in Kerala, historically performed for 28 days starting from Thiruvathira day.
It is closely linked to the Thiruvathira Vradam and the worship of Shiva and Parvati.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed during Onam and Thiruvathira day, the dance is believed to bring a long and auspicious married life.
It is also performed as Poothiruvathira by women after their marriage.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Indian Folk and Tribal Dance Performances (https://archive.org/details/dni.ncaa.ICCR-2088-VHS)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Women dance in a circle around a lit candle.
The movement involves rhythmic clapping of hands and simple steps performed to the beat of devotional songs.
Watch for Lasyabhava.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: circle around a lit candle
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music consists of devotional songs praising Shiva and Parvati.
The structure is a call-and-response format led by a heroine.
The music is defined by a lead singer performing the first line of a song, with the ensemble responding in unison while clapping.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear sarees and blouses.
The dance is performed at night, often in or near temples or homes, centered around a lit candle or lamp.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The dance is also known as Kaikottikali and Kummikali with slight variations.
A traditional Kerala dance form, classified as a group dance.

narration: The dance is performed as part of religious rituals in Shiva temples and is associated with the Thiruvathira Vradam.
